column3: The Hebrew says building Ramah and does not explicitly name territory; BSB uses fortifying and supplies territory.
The Hebrew describes Ben-hadad as dwelling in Damascus; BSB says ruling there.
The Hebrew gives the treaty as a nominal statement without an explicit let there be; BSB supplies that request.
The Hebrew has a separate plural striking verb and names stores of the cities; BSB uses conquering and store cities.
The Hebrew names all Judah; BSB supplies all the men of Judah.
The Hebrew repeats relying; BSB expresses the second occurrence elliptically.
The Hebrew says wars in the plural; BSB uses the state of being at war.
The Hebrew names a house of stocks and uses a crushing verb for Asa’s treatment of the people; BSB uses prison and oppressed.
The Hebrew twice says behold and has no separate rest of; BSB uses Now, indeed, and adds the rest of.
The Hebrew retains the image of the disease rising high; BSB interprets this as increasing severity.
The Hebrew first describes lying down with his fathers and then dying; BSB reverses this order and uses rested.
The Hebrew has plural graves and active plural buriers; BSB uses singular tomb and passive burial. The final burning expression repeats its root.
